candidates.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
candidates.task: occupation-specific professional writing tasks (press releases, short reports, analysis plans, delicate emails)
candidates.evidence: College-educated professionals (marketers, grant writers, consultants, data analysts, HR professionals, managers) were randomly given ChatGPT access before the second of two incentivized writing tasks; blinded evaluators from the same occupations graded overall quality and separate writing quality, content quality, and originality. Framed as a productivity study but originality is graded, so it may supply a with_ai originality estimate.

candidates.title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment
candidates.task: regular work of employees at a technology consulting firm
candidates.evidence: Employees of a technology consulting firm were randomly assigned to receive LLM (ChatGPT) assistance or not; employee creativity was rated by supervisors and by external evaluators, with metacognitive strategies as moderator. N=250 non-managerial employees comes from press summaries (Rice, PsyPost), not from the abstract.

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Roles of Generative AI in the Creative Process: Experiments on Design Work
candidates.task: design work at ideation and implementation stages; lab study with students and field study with professional designers
candidates.evidence: A lab experiment with students and a field experiment with professional designers compared design work with and without GenAI; work creativity rose with GenAI at the ideation stage for all, while expert designers gained no creativity and lost efficiency at implementation. Sample sizes and assignment method not confirmed (publisher page returned 403).

candidates.title: Unlocking creativity with artificial intelligence (AI): Field and experimental evidence on the Goldilocks (curvilinear) effect of human–AI collaboration
candidates.task: entrepreneurial challenge (business idea development) with ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Two experiments assigned 139 business professionals and 319 working adults to low, moderate, or high degrees of collaboration with ChatGPT; creativity was rated by human judges, business value by entrepreneurs, and creativity by AI, with moderate collaboration best via more diverse ideas. A multiwave survey of 188 creative-industry workers replicated the pattern. N counts the two experiments; random assignment is not stated in the summary found.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Ideation and the performance of Innovation Teams (Preprint)
candidates.task: team ideation on elderly-healthcare innovations and automotive business-model innovations
candidates.evidence: Framed field experiment: 70 business, economics, and information-systems students were randomly assigned to a GPT-4 Turbo ideation tool or no AI and worked in 24 three-person teams; blinded experts rated idea quality on Dean et al. dimensions including originality, and idea diversity and speed were compared. Student sample framed as innovation teams.

candidates.title: Don't Stop Sketching! Design Ideation Processes in the Age of Generative AI
other_versions: Lehmann (2026) PhD thesis, On the Effects of Complementary and Substitutive Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Innovation Processes, University of Cologne, urn:nbn:de:hbz:38-798064 (appears to contain this study)
candidates.task: design ideation with manual sketching before or instead of generative-AI image generation
candidates.evidence: According to the abstract of the related thesis, frontloading manual sketching before generative-AI use induced design fixation and lower idea variance but significantly higher design quality than AI-led ideation. The SSRN abstract was not retrievable (403), so design, sample, and assignment are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Generative AI Enhances Team Performance and Reduces Need for Traditional Teams
candidates.task: team content creation (articles on student job hunting) and a digital-transformation strategy for a retail chain
candidates.evidence: Preregistered RCT: 435 participants (professionals in operations, technology research, and general management, plus college students) randomly allocated to 122 teams assigned to human-only, single-AI, or multiple-AI (ChatGPT-4) conditions; a second experiment had 139 individuals paired with AI. Blind online judges rated each output on overall quality, novelty, and usefulness.

candidates.title: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work
candidates.task: marketing campaign for a fictional startup
candidates.evidence: 331 participants were randomized to a generic, partially personalized, or fully personalized LLM assistant; personalized AI produced marketing campaigns of higher rated quality and creativity. AI-configuration comparison with no stated no-AI arm; participant population not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Why unequal AI access enhances team productivity: the mediating role of interaction processes and cognitive diversity
other_versions: doi 10.1002/pra2.1437 (ASIS&T 2025 short paper: Unequal AI Access Enhances Team Productivity through Negative Socio-emotional Reactions and Cognitive Diversity)
candidates.task: two-person team press release for a hypothetical product
candidates.evidence: 120 university students in 60 two-person teams wrote a press release without AI, then teams were randomly assigned to unequal (one member) or full (both members) GenAI access; nine marketing professionals graded writing quality, content quality, and originality. Unequal access yielded the highest task quality.

candidates.title: Beyond Black Boxes: Designing and Testing Agentic AI Systems for Strategy
candidates.task: strategic challenge: building theories of value
candidates.evidence: RCT with 976 managers trained in theory-based strategy compared an agentic multi-agent AI system, general AI assistance, and no AI; experts and LLMs rated the quality and probability of success of participants' theories, which AI did not raise on average while confidence rose. Idea-quality outcome; creativity is not named explicitly.

candidates.title: Can large language models help young researchers develop new clinical research ideas?
candidates.task: generating ophthalmology clinical research ideas (from a topic, after reading a paper, in group discussion)
candidates.evidence: Compared research ideas from young researchers alone (n=3), LLMs alone (GPT-4o, Llama 3.1, Gemma 2), and researchers assisted by LLMs; 15 masked expert reviewers scored overall quality plus novelty, impact, relevance, feasibility, clarity, and completeness, and LLM-assisted researchers scored higher overall. Very small sample; registered ChiCTR2500097263.

candidates.title: Enhancing designer creativity through human–AI co-ideation: a co-creation framework for design ideation with custom GPT
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39
candidates.task: product design ideation (trash can, blender, alarm clock)
candidates.evidence: Validation study with 48 industrial-design master's students: 24 ideated with a custom GPT (Co-Ideator) and 24 without AI; ideas rated for novelty and quality were higher with the custom GPT, with no difference in variety. Assignment method not stated.

candidates.title: Analogical reasoning with large language models: a co-creative framework and benchmarking of LLMs in design ideation
candidates.task: design ideation on everyday-experience problem statements
candidates.evidence: 24 first-year design students ideated with or without an analogical LLM ideation agent (ALIA); six industry-experienced raters scored novelty, quality, and elaboration, and the AI-assisted group produced higher-rated ideas. A related earlier tool chapter is Kokate, Kompella, Onkar (2025), doi 10.1007/978-981-96-5495-6_46.

candidates.title: A novel idea generation tool using a structured conversational AI (CAI) system
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39: e11
candidates.task: design ideation on several design problems
candidates.evidence: Pilot study in which 30 novice designers generated ideas with traditional methods and with an LLM-based conversational ideation interface; an expert panel compared fluency, novelty, and variety, favoring the AI-enabled sessions.

candidates.title: Generative AI-Enabled Conceptualization: Charting ChatGPT's Impacts on Sustainable Service Design Thinking With Network-Based Cognitive Maps
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 25(2)
candidates.task: sustainable service concept design
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiments with 36 novice designers using ChatGPT, Tiangong AI, or no tool; design outcomes were evaluated, and ChatGPT raised concept novelty and systematicity but had limited effect on originality and sustainability.

candidates.title: How generative AI supports human in conceptual design
candidates.authors: Chen, Song, Guo, Sun, Childs, Yin
candidates.task: two conceptual design tasks
candidates.evidence: Novice designers completed two design tasks with or without generative AI; the abstract reports which design stages AI supports and improved idea selection and evaluation. Whether output creativity was rated is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Inkspire: Supporting Design Exploration with Generative AI through Analogical Sketching
candidates.authors: Lin, Kang, Martelaro, Kittur, Chen, Hong
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: product design concept prototyping with text-to-image AI
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study with product designers comparing a sketch-based analogical text-to-image tool with ControlNet; reports more inspiration and exploration of design ideas with the new tool. AI-configuration comparison; outcomes appear process and self-report based; N not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Exploring the impact of AI features on collaborative creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Australasian Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (OzCHI 2024): 480-489
candidates.task: pair ideation in a digital collaboration tool
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 36 participants in pairs using a digital whiteboard with or without AI features for divergent thinking, sense-making, and convergence; AI pairs produced more novel but less appropriate ideas, though differences were not statistically significant.

candidates.title: Augmented Learning for Joint Creativity in Human-GenAI Co-Creation
candidates.task: repeated human–GenAI co-creation tasks
candidates.evidence: Studies of human–GenAI co-creation find joint creativity does not improve over time by default, and that brief explanations and examples of Idea Co-Development (critical feedback exchange and joint refinement) significantly raise joint creativity. Design and N not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: Reviving Reflection-in-Action: Instilling Designerly Thinking in AI-Supported Ideation through Multimodal Prompting
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Creativity and Cognition (C&C '26)
candidates.task: design ideation with an AI creativity support tool (SketchifAI)
candidates.evidence: Within-participants study with design students comparing text, sketch, and sketch-plus-tags prompting of an AI tool; divergent-thinking performance (fluency, variety, originality, quality) was measured, with sketch input tending to raise fluency and inconclusive differences in originality. AI-configuration comparison.

candidates.title: Exploration vs. Fixation: Scaffolding Divergent and Convergent Thinking for Human-AI Co-Creation with Generative Models
candidates.task: creative poster image creation
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study (N=24) comparing a co-creation system with separate divergent and convergent modes (HAICo) against ChatGPT; HAICo outperformed ChatGPT on several creativity dimensions. AI-configuration comparison.

candidates.title: Creo: From One-Shot Image Generation to Progressive, Co-Creative Ideation
candidates.authors: De Simone, Boggust, Durand, Wilson, Satyanarayan
candidates.task: visual ideation with text-to-image generation
candidates.evidence: Comparative study of a staged sketch-to-image system against a one-shot text-to-image baseline; reports stronger ownership and an embedding-based analysis of outputs. The abstract was truncated in the record retrieved, so the direction of the diversity result is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: FocusGen: Expanding Visual Design Exploration with a Simulated Focus Group of Persona Agents
candidates.authors: Choi, Vasconcelos, Lee, Zou, Lee, Bernstein
candidates.task: visual design exploration for a design brief
candidates.evidence: System paper: persona agents built from preference interviews drive parallel text-to-image generation; with human participants the iterative loop produced preferred outputs, and visual diversity (CLIP distance, human judgments) exceeded a generic-assistant baseline, mostly shown with synthetic agents. Weak fit, included for the diversity outcome.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a cognitive support tool in early-stage design ideation: A human–AI co-ideation experiment
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation on one design brief
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment with 32 undergraduate design students comparing a text-and-image AI-assisted workflow with human-only brainstorming; three expert raters scored outputs: AI-assisted outputs rated higher on problem framing and perspective criteria, human-only outputs higher on innovation and proposed solution strategies.

candidates.title: Generative AI: A double-edged sword for creative thinking learning — Evidence from facial expressions and fNIRS
candidates.task: creative thinking tasks across stages of the creative process
candidates.evidence: Experiment with 128 participants from various academic backgrounds using generative AI during creative-thinking tasks, with fNIRS and facial-expression measures; GenAI raised creativity output scores with stage-dependent effects. Learner sample (outside this lane); N and design from a university news release.

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human–AI Co-Creation
candidates.task: alternate uses, consequences, and problem-solving tasks
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment with 202 German participants in human–human dyads, human–internet, and two human–AI (ChatGPT) conditions; human dyads scored higher on divergent-thinking tasks than the other groups, with no differences in problem solving. General-population sample (outside this lane).

candidates.title: Is ChatGPT detrimental to innovation? A field experiment among university students
candidates.task: graded essays with or without ChatGPT, then an unaided innovation game (lemonade-stand strategies)
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered field experiment in Egypt with nearly 100 senior university students: the treatment group wrote three graded essays with ChatGPT and the control group without; one week later both played an unaided innovation game, and the ChatGPT group was significantly less innovative. Relevant to after_ai; random assignment not stated in the abstract; student sample.

candidates.title: Empowering Engineering Students Through Artificial Intelligence (AI): Blended Human–AI Creative Ideation Processes With ChatGPT
candidates.task: creative ideation in a third-year engineering course
candidates.evidence: Randomized controlled experiment with third-year engineering students (728 ideas) on ChatGPT-assisted versus unassisted ideation, plus a survey; the abstract stresses perceptions, and idea-level creativity scoring is likely but not confirmed. Different paper from the collected Baltà-Salvador (2026) crossover study.

candidates.title: Rapid AIdeation: Generating Ideas With the Self and in Collaboration With Large Language Models
candidates.task: rapid ideation workshop on practical issues
candidates.evidence: Workshop with 21 participants who generated ideas themselves and with an LLM and evaluated them; LLM ideas were more varied and of high quality but not of higher quality than human ideas. No randomized comparison.

candidates.title: The Ink Splotch Effect: A Case Study on ChatGPT as a Co-Creative Game Designer
candidates.task: game features and game feel for three prototype games
candidates.evidence: For three genres, a base game, a version with features added by a human game designer, and a version with features taken directly from ChatGPT were blindly evaluated by users for quality and preference.

candidates.title: AI-Augmented Brainwriting: Investigating the use of LLMs in group ideation
candidates.authors: Shaer, Cooper, Mokryn, Kun, Ben Shoshan
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24): 1-17
candidates.task: group brainwriting ideation
candidates.evidence: An LLM was integrated into group brainwriting and the ideation process and resulting solution space were evaluated; an LLM idea-evaluation engine was compared with ratings by three expert and six novice evaluators. Presence of a no-AI control is unclear from the abstract.

candidates.title: Co-Ideation Across Dimensions: The Effects of Mediation Mode on Creative Collaboration and Ai Co-Ideation
candidates.task: group ideation with an AI co-ideation peer under different mediation modes
candidates.evidence: Title indicates an experiment varying the mediation mode of group collaboration with an AI co-ideation peer, by the group-AI brainwriting team with additional co-authors including Sadun. Abstract not retrieved (SSRN 403), so design, sample, and outcomes are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Research Novelty in Information Systems Journals After ChatGPT: Differences Across Institutional Language Contexts
candidates.task: 13,847 articles in 44 Information Systems journals, 2020-2025
candidates.evidence: Measures abstract-level semantic novelty (SPECTER2 distance from recent predecessors) before and after ChatGPT; articles from non-English-dominant institutions show a 0.176 SD larger post-2022 novelty decline. Individual LLM use is not observed.

candidates.title: Introducing AI to an online petition platform changed outputs but not outcomes
candidates.task: 1.5 million Change.org petitions around the launch of an in-platform write-with-AI tool
candidates.evidence: Difference-in-differences on 1.5 million petitions plus an analysis of repeat petition writers: in-platform AI access changed lexical features and increased petition homogeneity without improving petition outcomes. Published in Nature Human Behaviour on 2026-09-30.

candidates.title: Converging Naming Styles, Persistent Network Locality: GitHub in the LLM Era
candidates.task: identifier naming styles in public GitHub repositories created 2015 to September 2025
candidates.evidence: Repositories with detected LLM-related commits use longer identifiers and more already-prevalent naming patterns, and naming-style diversity falls in 2023-2024 creation cohorts in several languages, while network-local variation persists. Code-style homogenization rather than idea diversity.

candidates.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture: AI Homogenizes Syntax, Not (Necessarily) Semantics
candidates.task: Kaggle contest code submissions, 2019 to mid-2026
candidates.evidence: Within-contest similarity of Kaggle submissions measured with TF-IDF n-grams (syntax) and code embeddings (approach): submissions converge on seed 42 and in literal syntax but show no homogenization in approach or intent.

candidates.title: The Impact of Large Language Models on Open-source Innovation: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
candidates.task: open-source contributions to Python versus R packages around Copilot's launch
candidates.evidence: Natural experiment using Copilot's support for Python but not R: Copilot raised contributions by 28-40 percent, concentrated in incremental maintenance contributions rather than substantive, capability-extending ones. Innovation-type outcome rather than rated creativity.

candidates.title: Impact of LLM-Assisted Coding in Creativity and Robustness of Robot Controllers
candidates.venue: HAIC 2025, First International Workshop on Human-AI Collaborative Systems, CEUR Workshop Proceedings Vol-4072
candidates.task: programming robot controllers in a university course
candidates.evidence: Compares robot controllers produced by course students with and without LLM coding assistants; creativity is operationalized as structural diversity, and LLM-assisted controllers were more homogeneous and less robust. Assignment and N not confirmed from the first page.

candidates.title: "Like Taking the Path of Least Resistance": Exploring the Impact of LLM Interaction on the Creative Process of Programming
candidates.task: open-ended programming problems
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study with 20 programmers (LLM-assisted vs unassisted) plus interviews: LLM use shortened idea-generation periods and reduced creative moments, and solutions contained about the same number of ideas as unassisted ones.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and Strategic Decision-Making: Evidence from Entrepreneurs and Investors
other_versions: AEA RCT Registry AEARCTR-0011942 (pre-registration of the generation experiment)
candidates.task: business-plan strategies from an accelerator and a startup competition
candidates.evidence: Investors rated business plans whose strategy section was either the entrepreneur's original or GPT-generated (writing, innovation, execution, investment potential, viability), and LLM strategies were comparable to entrepreneurs'. No entrepreneur received AI help; the registry lists about 250 investor raters.

candidates.title: An Exploratory Research on Using Generative AI to Generate Print Ads
candidates.task: print advertisements in three contexts
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4 print ads were compared with human-developed ads: advertising professionals rated creativity and consumers rated effectiveness; professionals rated GenAI ads generally inferior in creativity for complex designs such as humor, while consumers found them comparable or sometimes better.

candidates.title: The power of generative marketing: Can generative AI create superhuman visual marketing content?
candidates.venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing 42(1): 13-31
candidates.task: marketing images: 10,320 images from seven text-to-image models versus human-made images; banner-ad field test
candidates.evidence: Compares AI-generated marketing images with human-made images and commissioned freelancer work on quality, realism, and aesthetics, plus a banner-ad click-through field test; AI images often matched or surpassed human ones. Creativity is not the main outcome.

candidates.title: Comparing the Ideation Quality of Humans With Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.task: new product and service ideas from human professionals versus an AI system
candidates.evidence: Blind expert evaluation of ideas generated by human professionals and by an AI system: AI ideas scored higher on novelty and customer benefit with similar feasibility and made up most of the top-rated ideas.

candidates.title: The rise of AI-enabled new product ideation: End of innovation crowdsourcing?
candidates.task: new product features from LLMs versus innovation-crowdsourcing ideas
candidates.evidence: Compares AI-generated product features with crowdsourced human ideas through the concept of AI-conceivability and their potential market value. Details come from the AMCIS 2024 abstract; the DSS abstract was not retrieved.

candidates.title: Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of ASME IDETC-CIE 2023, Volume 6: 35th International Conference on Design Theory and Methodology (DTM)
candidates.task: solutions to 12 engineering design problems: LLM versus crowdsourced
candidates.evidence: LLM-generated solutions to 12 design problems were compared with crowdsourced human solutions using expert ratings and computational metrics; LLM solutions had higher feasibility and usefulness, crowdsourced solutions more novelty.

candidates.title: Do Large Language Models Produce Diverse Design Concepts? A Comparative Study with Human-Crowdsourced Solutions
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 25(2)
other_versions: arXiv 2405.02345 (preprint titled 'Exploring the Capabilities of Large Language Models for Generating Diverse Design Solutions'; seen in search results, not verified through the API)
candidates.task: design solutions on five topics: 4,000 GPT-4 solutions versus 100 crowdsourced solutions per topic
candidates.evidence: Diversity metrics compared between GPT-4 design solutions (varying parameters and prompting techniques) and human crowdsourced solutions; human solutions were consistently more diverse.

candidates.title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
candidates.task: executing NLP research ideas written by experts or generated by an LLM
candidates.evidence: 43 expert researchers each executed a randomly assigned research idea (expert-written or LLM-generated) and wrote a short paper reviewed blind; LLM ideas lost more than expert ideas on novelty, excitement, effectiveness, and overall scores after execution. Follow-up to the collected Si et al. ideation study.

candidates.title: Art or Artifice? Large Language Models and the False Promise of Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24): 1-34
candidates.task: short stories by professional authors versus LLMs
candidates.evidence: Ten creative writers applied the Torrance Test of Creative Writing (fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration) to 48 stories by professional authors or LLMs; LLM stories passed 3-10 times fewer tests.

candidates.title: Readers Prefer Outputs of AI Trained on Copyrighted Books over Expert Human Writers
candidates.task: 450-word excerpts emulating 50 award-winning authors: MFA-trained writers versus frontier models
candidates.evidence: Preregistered blind pairwise evaluations by 28 MFA-trained readers and 516 general readers compared excerpts by MFA-trained writers and by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini; prompted AI text was disfavored by experts on style fidelity and quality, while author-specific fine-tuning reversed the result.

candidates.title: Pron vs Prompt: Can Large Language Models already Challenge a World-Class Fiction Author at Creative Text Writing?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP): 19654-19670
candidates.task: short stories by novelist Patricio Pron versus GPT-4 on 60 titles
candidates.evidence: Pron and GPT-4 each proposed 30 titles and wrote stories for all 60; literature critics and scholars gave 5,400 assessments on a Boden-inspired creativity rubric, and GPT-4 fell well short of the novelist. Author list follows Crossref (the fourth author appears on arXiv as Ramón del Castillo).

candidates.title: LLMs Exhibit Significantly Lower Uncertainty in Creative Writing Than Professional Writers
candidates.task: human-authored stories versus continuations from 28 LLMs
candidates.evidence: Information-theoretic comparison shows human creative writing has significantly higher uncertainty than LLM continuations, with larger gaps for instruction-tuned and reasoning models; model-versus-human output comparison with no human participants assisted.

candidates.title: Expertise Elevates AI Usage: Experimental Evidence Comparing Laypeople and Professional Artists
candidates.authors: Eisenmann, Karjus, Canet Sola, Brinkmann, Supriyatno, Rahwan
candidates.task: image replication and creative image creation with a text-to-image platform
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered comparison of 50 professional artists and matched laypeople using the same text-to-image AI: artists made more accurate copies and more divergent creative images, and GPT-4o acting alone did slightly better than artists on average in the creative task. Both groups used AI, so no no-AI baseline; total N not stated.

candidates.title: Psittacines of Innovation? Assessing the True Novelty of AI Creations
candidates.task: crowdfunding project titles: AI-generated versus actual field data
candidates.evidence: Compares AI-generated crowdfunding project titles with observed real titles using a kernel embedding discrepancy measure, finding unique and divergent AI content. Mostly model output against real human output; weak fit.

candidates.title: Contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science
candidates.authors: Bao, Wu, Liu, Li, Cao, Evans
candidates.task: LLM-generated research ideas derived from scientists' own preprints, rated by those scientists
candidates.evidence: 6,749 scientists returned 25,139 ratings of LLM ideas on novelty, feasibility, truth, and adoption; non-reasoning LLMs collapse into a narrow hivemind of similar ideas and no model proposes null hypotheses, a move humans make more freely. Mainly a model evaluation with human raters; N counts raters, so left null.

candidates.title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
candidates.task: idea generation by independent human samples versus independent LLM samples
candidates.evidence: Four studies show LLM idea sets are less diverse than human idea sets because of fixation and the lack of knowledge partitioning; Chain-of-Thought prompting plus ordinary personas raised LLM idea diversity above human levels.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: creative writing with interactive AI assistance
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered RCT randomizing incentives (rewards for originality relative to peers versus quality alone) in a writing task where participants could use AI; originality incentives produced collectively more diverse writing, with fewer AI suggestions used verbatim. Randomization is over incentives, not AI access.

candidates.title: AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
candidates.task: new product ideas for college students priced under 50 dollars: LLM versus human ideas
candidates.evidence: Series of studies: LLM product ideas have higher average quality (purchase intent) but lower idea-level novelty and set-level diversity than human ideas; pooling vendors, prompting, personas, and agents restore diversity. Appears to consolidate the collected Girotra et al. (2023) and Meincke et al. (2024) work; report as a possible newer version.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as an inventor: eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39
candidates.task: 48-hour engineering prototyping hackathon
candidates.evidence: A ChatGPT-4-directed team (two participants executing its instructions) competed against graduate engineering student teams in a prototyping hackathon with over 100 prototypes; the LLM team finished second of six, showed strong concept generation but also design fixation.

candidates.title: AI-powered inventive design: idea funnelling, concept creation, and hybrid problem-solving teams
candidates.task: engineering inventive design problems
candidates.evidence: Comparative experiments on AI-powered idea funnelling (ChatGPT, Gemini) and hybrid AI-human problem-solving teams, assessing feasibility, contextual relevance, and innovation quality of concepts. Conditions and sample are not detailed in the abstract.

candidates.title: Case study: is there a space for TRIZ in the era of ChatGPT?
candidates.task: industrial product development problem solving
candidates.evidence: Industrial case study comparing team-generated solutions with solutions from LLMs and TRIZ-enhanced LLMs. Earlier, separate paper from the collected Čok (2026) TRIZ experiment.

candidates.title: Hack-Agents: A Multi-Agent System for Innovation - Proof of Concept and Implications for AI-Augmented Hackathons
candidates.venue: Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems: 1-6
candidates.task: innovation hackathons with phase-specific multi-agent AI assistance
candidates.evidence: A phase-specific multi-agent LLM system (ideation feedback, implementation chatbot, evaluation prompts) designed to avoid premature convergence and loss of idea diversity was deployed in two innovation hackathons, a pilot and a follow-up study. Comparison conditions and outcomes were truncated in the abstract retrieved.

candidates.title: In Search of "Weird Corners": Diagnosing the Limits of Convergent AI in Professional Creative Practice
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition: 1582-1587
candidates.task: expert creatives using a convergent AI probe
candidates.evidence: Probe study with nine expert creatives finds convergent AI assistance helps early ideation but induces aesthetic sanitization that standardizes individual nuance. Qualitative; no rated outcome; included because it concerns convergence among professionals.

candidates.title: From Play to Performance: Creating with AI in Personal Life as a Source of Work Creativity
candidates.task: employees' personal-life AI-assisted creating and later workplace creativity
candidates.evidence: Multi-wave field study in two companies plus an online experiment: personal-life AI-assisted creating predicts higher workplace creativity through motivational routes. Spillover rather than AI removal at measurement; experimental manipulation and creativity measure unclear from the conference abstract.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence, Scientific Discovery, and Product Innovation
candidates.task: materials discovery by R&D scientists with an AI tool
candidates.evidence: WITHDRAWN by arXiv administrators in May 2025 due to concerns about the validity of the data and incomplete IRB requirements. It claimed AI-assisted researchers discovered more materials with more novel structures and more radical inventions. Listed only so screeners can exclude it knowingly.

candidates.title: The effect of Generative AI on Early Stage Business Ideas: An Experimental Approach
candidates.task: early-stage venture ideas by engineering-student entrepreneur groups
candidates.evidence: Registered RCT (intervention August 2024 to August 2026) randomizing at least 130 groups of 4-5 to training in generative-AI use for business development versus traditional creativity-tool training; outcomes are judges' grades of problem relevance and value proposition plus market traction. Registration only; no results found.
